correctness.rationale: The two-cycle exclusion integrates the Hessian of the weighted sine potential and uses a strict Laplacian Rayleigh bound; coordinate displacement below 2 radians per update eliminates torus winding artifacts for the range claimed. Perron--Frobenius simplicity on bipartite graphs, Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction, and positive quartic edge coefficient yield the supercritical antipodal branch. Explicit Jacobian perturbation makes it a transverse sink, and odd center manifold dynamics at the threshold gives the universal generic reciprocal-time squared-norm limit. The packaged script independently computes positive edge energies, branch residuals, multipliers and critical constants on several graphs. Finite computation is corroborative rather than a universal certificate.

value.rationale: This natural network class has arbitrary topology within connected bipartite graphs and arbitrary positive edge weights, so the transition organizes genuinely different spatial mode profiles. The exact global obstruction before the threshold and locally attracting period-two pattern after it identify the precise discretization-induced oscillation boundary, while the critical asymptotic provides a universal graph-dependent timescale. Neither a mere eigenvalue stability test nor an arbitrary finite numerical observation supplies the three-part theorem.
